steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Charts and diagrams are visual representations of data that make it easier to understand patterns, trends, and comparisons.

steps.title: Features
steps.body: Bars have equal width Height represents frequency or value Gaps between bars (discrete data) Both axes should be labelled

steps.title: Key Facts
steps.body: A full circle = 360° Each sector represents a category Angle for each category = (frequency ÷ total) × 360°

steps.title: Features
steps.body: Use symbols or pictures to represent data Include a key showing what each symbol represents Can use half-symbols for half values

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Calculate the angle for a pie chart sector representing 15 students out of a total of 60. | A pictogram uses ⭐ = 6 points. How many stars are needed to represent 27 points? | In a bar chart, what should be the height of the "Blue" bar if 24 people chose blue out of 120 surveyed?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: (15/60) × 360° = 90° | 27 ÷ 6 = 4.5 stars (4 full stars and 1 half star) | Height = 24 (the frequency value)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always label axes and include a title Check pie chart angles add up to 360° Include a key for pictograms For bar charts, ensure bars have equal width with gaps Look for trends and patterns in time series Read the scale carefully - don't assume it starts at 0
